# Chapter 67

“Ugh, every bone in my body aches.”

Hyuk Mujin groaned. His bare upper body was covered in dark reddish-black bruises.

At the sight, the crotchety-looking old man—the Medicine King Hall Master—clicked his tongue.

“What the hell did you do to your body?”

He untied the bundle he had brought with him, revealing acupuncture needles as thick as stakes. Hyuk Mujin asked in a terrified voice, “You’re going to stick those in me?”

“What, scared?”

“They look like they’ll hurt like hell… Please go easy on me.”

“Sure.”

The Medicine King Hall Master answered readily and took out two large needles.

“I’ll put one in the crown of your head and one in your perineum. If you die, you won’t have to worry about pain anymore.”

“……”

“Now you’re ready for treatment.”

Having silenced Hyuk Mujin with a single sentence, the Medicine King Hall Master got to work. In the blink of an eye, dozens of needles, large and small, pierced Hyuk Mujin’s skin.

Thuk-thuk-thuk.

“Argh! Argh!”

“A young punk like you, making such a fuss. From the sound of those lungs, you’ll be hale and hearty for another fifty years.”

Leaving the now porcupine-like Hyuk Mujin behind, the Medicine King Hall Master turned to me.

“Strip.”

“W-What?”

“Are you deaf? Take off your shirt.”

When age entered the equation, being the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi could go straight to hell. I eyed the blue-glinting needles and took off my shirt.

Rustle.

“Hm?”

The Medicine King Hall Master’s eyes widened when he saw my body.

“What the hell are you?”

His voice was full of astonishment, and understandably so. Until yesterday, my body had been covered in bruises. Now, my skin was completely clear.

*I didn’t expect this much either.*

After a single night’s sleep, most of the bruises had disappeared, and even my aching bones felt perfectly fine.

*Is this the power of Sleep Mode?*

Apparently, simply sleeping was now enough for me to recover quickly from most ordinary bruises. Even the Medicine King Hall Master, a physician seasoned by years of experience, found me so remarkable that he examined me for quite some time.

“Did you take an elixir last night?”

“No. I just circulated my qi all day and got a good night’s sleep.”

“Could it be the hundred-year snow ginseng? No, this is too much…”

The Medicine King Hall Master glared at me suspiciously, as though wondering whether I had raided the medicine storeroom again, then shook his head.

“The Third Young Master may be discharged.”

Hyuk Mujin, who had been groaning, immediately brightened.

“What about me? What about me?”

“I swear, if you run off again without permission, I’ll ram one of these needles into your perineum.”

The gaunt old man muttered in a sinister voice, jabbing a large needle through the air. He looked like something straight out of a horror movie.

*That’ll be one bloody opening ceremony.*

“Third Young Master, get out. Unless you want the needles too.”

*Thank you…*

I sprang to my feet, eager to escape those eyes gleaming with madness.

Then a sudden realization struck me.

*Where am I supposed to go now?*

The pavilion had collapsed, leaving me with nowhere to return to. I had become homeless overnight, and as I stood there hesitating—

“Ahem. Medicine King Hall Master, are you inside?”

A familiar voice came from beyond the door. Wondering if it could really be him, I opened it and found exactly the face I had expected.

“Hyung?”

Jin Wikyung jumped a beat too late.

“What are you doing here? I happened to stop by in the middle of my duties because I had urgent business with the Medicine King Hall Master. What an incredible coincidence!”

“……”

*Nice try.*

* * *

After hearing about my situation, Jin Wikyung led the way with a solemn expression.

“I know somewhere you can stay for a while. Follow me.”

He was clearly conscious of the people watching us. After all, the image he had built over the years was that of a coolheaded, capable Lesser Family Head who kept public and private matters strictly separate.

The problem was…

“It’s the Lesser Family Head.”

“Isn’t that the Third Young Master beside him? What are those two doing together in broad daylight?”

“Maybe he can’t bear to be apart from him for even a moment. You know how he dotes on the Third Young Master.”

Everyone who paid any attention already knew the truth: Jin Wikyung was a complete sucker for his little brother.

*Of course they know. Anyone who doesn’t would be the strange one.*

He was still like this in his mid-thirties. I could only imagine how bad he had been when he was younger. Right after the battle, he had even been so overcome with joy that he carried me around on his shoulders.

*My youngest! My little brother!*

After making that kind of spectacle in front of hundreds of people, there was no way anyone could have missed it.

As I sighed inwardly, a thread of Sound Transmission slipped into my ear.

—How was that? Hyung can act too, huh?

I nodded. If there were an Academy Award for terrible acting, he might have had a shot at Best Actor.

—Are you feeling all right? Mukyung didn’t do it out of malice, so I hope you’ll understand.

“……”

There had been plenty of malice in those fists. It was only thanks to my rapid recovery that I hadn’t spent the next several days staring at the Medicine King Hall ceiling.

*I should avoid running into him whenever possible.*

He was young, ill-tempered, and had the martial arts to back it up. There was no dealing with him.

The moment Jin Mukyung appeared, he had shot straight to the top of my internal watch list.

“Still, see him often enough and you’ll grow fond of him.”

*See him often enough and I’ll grow black-and-blue.*

Oblivious to my thoughts, Jin Wikyung laughed heartily and continued walking.

We passed through the bustling heart of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and kept going. The farther we went, the fewer people we saw.

*Where are we now?*

The sheer size of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s estate spoke to its former glory. Even from a distance, it looked as large as several soccer fields combined, so it was only natural that I had never explored all of it. Everywhere I went, I still found places I had never seen before.

*Everything’s run-down.*

By now, the people had disappeared completely, leaving the road deserted. The occasional pavilion and other buildings whose purposes I couldn’t identify were old and gloomy.

It had the kind of atmosphere where rats held sports festivals during the day and ghosts played go-stop at night.[^1]

When I looked around, Jin Wikyung hurriedly began to explain.

“Given the state our family has been in, maintaining even this much was more than we could manage. Now we’ll have to undertake extensive renovations, of course.”

“I don’t really mind.”

“Really?”

“Yes.”

I meant it.

I had survived five whole years in a cramped, three-pyeong goshiwon studio.[^2] Rats could be caught, and as for ghosts… Well, it wasn’t as though real ghosts would actually show up.

“As long as it’s spacious, I’m fine.”

“So you don’t care about anything else, as long as it’s spacious?”

That phrasing sounded slightly ominous, but I nodded anyway. Jin Wikyung’s face brightened.

“That’s a relief. I was worried you might not like it.”

“Where exactly is this place?”

“We’re here. This is the building.”

“Oh.”

We stopped in front of a large three-story pavilion. Compared to the other buildings we had passed, it was much cleaner and possessed a distinctly elegant, old-fashioned charm.

I also liked the tall stone wall surrounding it.

“It’s nice.”

There was absolutely no reason to dislike a place like this.

Jin Wikyung smiled brightly, clearly pleased by my reaction.

“Do you like it?”

“Yes. It’s much cleaner than I expected, and it looks incredibly spacious.”

“That’s right. I had the training hall built large.”

“A training hall!”

“I had another one built underground in case the weather was bad.”

“Oh! Two training halls!”

“If you divide them between you, there shouldn’t be any problem.”

“Whoa. If we divide them, that’d be perfect… Huh?”

Wait. What had he just said?

“I’m not using this place alone?”

“Oh, well…”

Jin Wikyung smiled awkwardly.

“It’s spacious enough for two people, isn’t it? You might even grow closer while you’re at it.”

“Who is it?”

Unease began creeping up my spine.

And bad premonitions were never wrong.

Instead of answering, Jin Wikyung strode into the pavilion.

“Mukyung! Your big brother’s here!”

*Oh, damn it.*

* * *

“So, I’d like you two to live together until his residence is rebuilt.”

After hearing the situation, Jin Mukyung readily nodded.

“Very well.”

I hadn’t expected him to accept so readily.

His response surprised both Jin Wikyung and me.

“Wait, are you serious?”

“Yes. But please send me one person tomorrow.”

“Of course. I was worried about you shutting yourself away in the training hall all alone anyway, so this works out well. I’ll find you a capable servant who’s quick on the uptake. Or should I bring in a cook while I’m at it?”

“I don’t need a servant or a cook.”

“Then what?”

Jin Mukyung gave me a long, meaningful look.

“Call a physician.”

“……”

“……”

The scenery I had seen on the way here suddenly rose before my eyes.

Deserted streets. An underground training hall where no one would hear a scream. The perfect conditions for committing a crime.

*He’s made up his mind to beat me senseless.*

As a chill ran through me, Jin Wikyung stammered, “M-Mukyung. You don’t mean that, do you? It’s not what I’m thinking, right?”

“It’s exactly what you’re thinking. It might be worse.”

“If it’s worse…”

“Then you’ll need an undertaker instead of a physician.”

Without a moment’s hesitation, I hurled myself toward the exit.

Whoosh! Grab!

*Goddammit.*

Jin Wikyung caught me by the nape and hauled me back. Jin Mukyung let out a short laugh as he watched.

“What a pathetic movement technique. Even a back-alley dog would be faster than you.”

This time, I shot back.

“If it’s faster than me, is it really a dog? That’d be Red Hare.”[^3]

“Even after that beating, you still haven’t come to your senses.”

“Hit me! Come on, hit me!”

Of course, I had no intention of actually being hit. I had a dependable protector on my side.

“Enough!”

The booming shout shook the underground training hall. Jin Wikyung’s face had hardened, utterly unlike before.

“What do you two think you’re doing?”

I had never seen him like this. They said it was frightening when a kind person got angry, and Jin Wikyung now showed me exactly what that meant.

“You’re brothers. Instead of getting along, you’re trying to start a fight right in front of me?”

Under his fierce glare, Jin Mukyung and I both fell silent.

“It isn’t half a year or a year. It’s only fifteen days. I’m asking you to live together until the pavilion is rebuilt. Is that really such a difficult request?”

Jin Mukyung flinched. As the one responsible for demolishing the pavilion, he couldn’t help feeling guilty.

“That was because this brat was being rude…”

“And that gave you the right to demolish a pavilion and beat your little brother? You call that an excuse?”

Jin Mukyung lowered his head.

“I’m sorry.”

This time, the arrow turned toward me.

“Taekyung, what about you?”

I wanted to whip out my ID card, but I restrained myself.

This body was only twenty now, and Jin Mukyung was my blood brother, three years older than me.

“Answer me!”

“……I’m sorry.”

Jin Wikyung glared sternly at both of us.

“This is a decision I reached after careful consideration. If you dislike each other that much, say so now. I’ll respect your wishes.”

Jin Mukyung and I locked eyes.

Our answers came at the same time.

“I don’t want to.”

“Nor do I.”

“……”

After a heavy silence, Jin Wikyung finally managed to speak.

“I’m glad you two are willing to follow your big brother’s wishes.”

*Why ask when he’d already decided on the answer?*
